claim.pdf_says: Argument Type / Function type table, last row: "Numeric (some arguments may be integer)    Numeric"
claim.markdown_says:
| National | National |

   Numeric (some arguments may be integer) Numeric
claim.why_it_matters: The last row of the argument-type/function-type table is detached from the markdown table and rendered as a loose indented paragraph, so the table loses its Numeric row and the two columns of that row run together.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 697 (PDF p721), 15.59: the argument-type table has six rows, the last being 'Numeric (some arguments may be integer)' | 'Numeric', aligned in the same two columns as Alphabetic..National. The markdown table (page-721.md) ends at '| National | National |'; the sixth row follows after a blank line as an indented loose paragraph '   Numeric (some arguments may be integer) Numeric'. Both sources are quoted accurately. The words are present, so nothing is lost to a careful human reader, but the table structurally omits its Numeric row and the column boundary between argument type and function type is gone, so any reading of the table as a table (by a tool or a reader scanning rows) loses the numeric-argument -> numeric-function mapping. Genuine structural transcription defect, correctly classified as structural rather than normative.
